statement: When I encounter a technical issue I haven't seen before, I prefer to research solutions myself before asking my manager.
I often find it tedious to double-check my work if I feel confident I did it correctly the first time.
If a client sends an angry message regarding a delayed process, my immediate reaction is to escalate it to a supervisor rather than trying to de-escalate it first.
I feel comfortable managing my own schedule as long as I hit my daily KPIs and deadlines.
I rely on strict daily routines and detailed checklists to ensure I don't miss any steps in a multi-stage process.
When providing an update to the team, I prefer giving a brief, high-level summary rather than breaking down specific details.
If I notice a recurring inefficiency in our team's workflow, I will proactively suggest a new automation or process rather than just adapting to it.
I have occasionally submitted reports or data entries with minor typos because I was rushing to meet a deadline.
I am very careful about my tone in written messages to ensure I don't sound too blunt or demanding.
I prefer jobs where my tasks are explicitly laid out for me step-by-step every single day.
